title: perf(app-shell): destructure the one symbol the CEL bridge's dynamic core import uses (objectui#9492)
body:
Fixes #9492

## What changed

One line in the metadata-admin CEL authoring bridge, the docblock above it, and a changeset. Two files.

`loadRowCanon()` imported the `@object-ui/core` barrel dynamically and then returned the imported NAMESPACE object from its `.then` callback, caching it in a Promise. An escaping namespace is a live namespace, so rolldown had to retain every export of the barrel on the eager path: the specifier was dynamic and the payload was eager anyway. The callback now destructures `detectNonCanonicalRowSpelling` — the single member the local `RowCanonModule` interface declares, and the single member this file accesses — so only that binding escapes.

The docblock warned only about a STATIC import and was silent about the namespace case. It now states both halves, and records why a deep subpath is not the alternative: `packages/core`'s manifest declares only the `"."` export key (verified on this branch), so a subpath specifier is unreachable for a real consumer of the published package. The destructure is the form that works through the published barrel.

## Which build these figures are from

All byte figures are **console builds** — `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` — taken through this container's shared heavy-verify lock. That build aliases every workspace package to its own `src` (the alias table in the console's vite config), so these are source-tree readings and not readings of the published tarballs. Gzip is zlib level 6, the level the report emitter uses. Four console builds over two trees; every leg below is a real compile, none is a cache restore.

## Tree A — this branch's base, `main` at `c42554e94`

`pnpm check:eager-closure`, ablation leg (pre-change bytes) then this branch's bytes:

| | before | after | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| eager closure, gz | 3,139,738 | 3,122,006 | **-17,732** |
| `data-adapter`, gz | 78,821 | 44,523 | -34,298 |
| `framework`, gz | 47,906 | 68,389 | **+20,483** |
| `vendor-objectstack`, gz | 1,240,242 | 1,236,320 | -3,922 |
| gate exit code | **0** | **0** | |

Gate verdict lines, quoted:

- before: `Console eager closure is 3066.2 KB gzipped across 329 of 2309 chunks (budget: 3104.5 KB, headroom: 38.3 KB)` / `framework 46.8 KB / 97.7 KB ceiling (headroom 50.9 KB)`
- after: `Console eager closure is 3048.8 KB gzipped across 329 of 2309 chunks (budget: 3104.5 KB, headroom: 55.7 KB)` / `framework 66.8 KB / 97.7 KB ceiling (headroom 30.9 KB)`

⭐ **Read the `framework` row correctly, because it moves the "wrong" way here.** On `main` today the card's downstream repair has not landed, so `packages/core` is not grouped into `framework` yet — the modules this narrowing frees are sitting in the unbudgeted `data-adapter` chunk. Narrowing therefore drops 34,298 gz out of `data-adapter` while the chunker re-groups part of the remainder into `framework` (+20,483), for a net **-17,732** on the closure as a whole. Nothing crosses a ceiling in either direction, and no ceiling goes blind: the aggregate sensitivity row moves 0.43x → 0.63x of the 89.0 KB regression and `framework` 0.57x → 0.35x, both inside the band.

⛔ **The gate was already green on `main` before this change.** The card's own headline reading (exit 1, `OVER by 4.5 KB`) is a statement about the downstream repair's head, not about `main`, and this branch cannot reproduce it on `main`. So it was re-derived where it lives.

## Tree B — the downstream repair's head (read-only probe)

Measured in a throwaway worktree at that branch's head `d2ac39197`, with this branch's commit cherry-picked on top (it applies with no conflict; that branch does not touch this file — the blob is byte-identical to `main`'s). ⛔ Nothing was pushed, opened or otherwise written there.

| | repair alone | repair + this branch | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| eager closure, gz | 3,134,445 | 3,116,444 | **-18,001** |
| `framework`, gz | **104,636** | **90,540** | **-14,096** |
| `vendor-objectstack`, gz | 1,240,245 | 1,236,309 | -3,936 |
| `packages/core` modules in `framework` | **92** | **76** | -16 |
| gate exit code | **1** | **0** | |

Gate verdict lines, quoted:

- repair alone, exit 1: `1 eager chunk is over its per-chunk budget` / `framework 102.2 KB / 97.7 KB ceiling (OVER by 4.5 KB)`
- repair plus this branch, exit 0: `Per-chunk eager budgets (4 chunks weighed)` / `framework 88.4 KB / 97.7 KB ceiling (headroom 9.2 KB)`

The membership half stays green on both legs and the repair is not undone: `5 budgeted package(s) each landed wholly in their declared chunk`, with `packages/core` wholly inside `framework` on both — 92 modules before, 76 after.

⚠️ **One number worth the reviewer's eye.** On that combined tree `framework` lands at 9,460 bytes of headroom = **0.104x** of the 89.0 KB regression, against this gate's 0.10x exhausted-headroom floor of 9,113.6 bytes. It clears the floor by 346 bytes and the gate ticks it green, but it is the tightest of the five rows. That is the ceiling's business and not this card's; it is recorded here rather than acted on.

## Controls — every zero carries one

**Reconciliation.** Tree A: 26 of 329 eager chunks changed, the per-chunk deltas sum to exactly -17,732, equal to the report's own aggregate delta. Tree B: 23 of 329 changed, summing to exactly -18,001. **No chunk entered or left the closure** on either tree — both the before-only and after-only chunk-NAME sets are empty. That zero is not an empty run: the same set difference taken over chunk FILE names returns 31 and 31 on tree A, because content hashes move, so the instrument is demonstrably live in the direction that can return non-zero.

**Ablation, proven on disk rather than by an editor's exit code.** Both trees were measured the same way: commit the change, then restore the pre-change bytes with a path-scoped checkout against a pinned commit, prove the mutation reached the disk (`git hash-object` equals the pre-change blob, and the grep count for the namespace-cast anchor goes 0 to 1 while the destructure goes 1 to 0), build, read the gate; then restore, prove the restore the same way, and build again. Restore is proven by `git diff HEAD` and `git diff --cached` both returning zero lines, never by a command's exit status. Every mutating leg ran under a trap that restores on EXIT, INT and TERM, with absolute paths.

**Negative control — narrowed, not reverted.** The fence that matters here is that the lazy boundary stays lazy. After the change the dynamic specifier is still present and still dynamic in this file: one occurrence of the dynamic form, zero static imports of `@object-ui/core` in this file. What changed is what the callback NAMES. A revert would have removed the specifier or made it static; neither happened.

**Vacuity control on the covering suites.** `celAuthoring.test.ts` and `celAuthoring.fieldRuleVerdict-9318.test.ts` pass 51/51 with the narrowing applied. Renaming the destructured binding to a name the barrel does not export — proven on disk, then restored — takes the SAME command to `exit 1` with exactly 2 failures, and the restored tree returns to 51/51. So the suites really do exercise the narrowed symbol.

**Premise control on the call-site count.** The dynamic specifier appears 13 times in the tree outside `node_modules` and `dist`: 12 of them in 9 test files, exactly 1 in production — this one. The "exactly one" is a filter over a pattern that demonstrably matches 13 things, not a pattern that matches nothing.

## Fences

- ⛔ **No ceiling, baseline or budget constant is touched.** The diff is two files: this source file and a changeset. The gate flips on payload alone.
- ⛔ **The lazy import is narrowed, not reverted or disabled** — see the negative control above.
- ⛔ **No export key was added to `packages/core`** to make a subpath work. The destructure works through the barrel that is actually published.

## Gates run locally

| gate | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:eager-closure` | exit 0 on this branch; exit 1 then exit 0 on the downstream tree |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the two covering suites | exit 0, 51/51 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 1 without the changeset, exit 0 with it |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` and `check:changeset-claims` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0, 7786 tracked text files scanned |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | exit 0, 0 new citations |
| `eslint` over the changed file | exit 0, 1 file linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the changed path | NOT GOVERNED |

The lint reading is a declared narrowing: the repo-level scan is `turbo run lint` per package and belongs to CI. It is a measurement rather than a skipped run because type-aware linting is not enabled in this repo's eslint config (no `project` or `projectService` key in `languageOptions`; the TypeScript preset in use is the untyped `recommended` one), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The file count is read from eslint's own `--format json` output. Every reading above was taken at `d9c181bc2`, this branch's head.
